name: Hora, Spring
body:
SPRING HORA
CR 6

This beautiful woman dances among the flowers without leaving a trace; her hair, skin, and eyes match the green, gold, pink, and blue of a flowery meadow, as do the veils she wears.

XP 2,400
CG Medium fey
Init +8; Senses low-light vision; Perception +16
Aura charming beauty (30 ft., DC 19)

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 15, flat-footed 14 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +4 natural)
hp 65 (10d6+30); fast healing 5
Fort +6, Ref +11, Will +10; +4 vs. aging effects
DR 5/cold iron
Weaknesses spring bound

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee blooming quarterstaff +9 (3d6+3 bludgeoning +1d6 positive energy)
Ranged ray of life +9 (4d8 positive energy)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 10th; concentration +14)

Constant—speak with animals, speak with plants
At will—know direction, light, pass without trace
1/day—alarm, animal messenger, bestow curse (DC 18), commune with nature, entangle (DC 15)

STATISTICS

Str 12, Dex 19, Con 16, Int 15, Wis 17, Cha 18
Base Atk +5; CMB +6, CMD 21
Feats Combat Casting, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Mobility, Weapon Finesse
Skills Acrobatics +17, Diplomacy +17, Escape Artist +17, Knowledge (nature) +15, Perception +16, Sense Motive +16, Stealth +17, Survival +13
Languages Common, Elven, Sylvan; speak with animals, speak with plants
SQ spring’s safekeeping

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Charming Beauty (Su)

This ability affects all humanoids within 30 feet of the spring hora. Those who look directly at the hora must succeed on a DC 19 Fortitude save or be under the effect of charm monster for 1 minute and then fascinated for a maximum of 1 hour. The hora can suppress or resume this ability as a free action. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Spring Bound (Su)

During autumn months, the spring hora gains the sickened condition.

Spring’s Safekeeping (Su)

As an immediate action after a spring hora or an ally within 30 feet of the hora that it can see fails a saving throw, the hora grants an enhancement bonus to the saving throw based on the time of year. The bonus is +4 during the month of the vernal equinox, +2 during the month before or after the vernal equinox, and +1 during any time other than the autumnal equinox month, during which this ability doesn’t function. The spring hora can’t use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate forests
Organization solitary or chorus (2-12)
Treasure standard (blooming quarterstaff, other treasure)

The Horai in the Greek myth were nymphs who danced around the Sun’s chariot, representing the seasons of the year and the hours of the day (the word “hour” derives from the Ancient Greek and Latin Hora). There were most commonly three of them: Thallo, Auxo, and Carpo (“Bloom” for Spring, “Increaser” for Summer, and “Reaper of Fruits” for Autumn). In other versions, they were the embodiment of the good effects of law and order (symbolized by Apollo) on the world of mortals, and their names were Eunomia (“Good Governance”), Dike (“Justice”), and Eirene (“Peace”). In Pathfinder’s rules, the stats for the Summer Hora and the Summer Hora Queen were given in the Faerie Bestiary: here we present horai for the remaining three seasons, and their respective Queens. Maybe the nymphs of Order could be discussed in a future issue of this magazine?
